prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

Disclosed is a bottle trap having a main body having an open end coupled to a tailpiece pipe and a tapered closed end having at least one face inclined at a first angle with respect to axis of the main body. The bottle trap also includes a cylindrical trap element received on the open end and extending axially into the main body up to at least half the length of the main body. An outlet orifice is configured on peripheral surface of the main body perpendicularly thereto. The outlet orifice is adapted to be coupled to a horizontal drain pipe. Also, a thread-less coupling is configured at the open end and outlet orifice, respectively, for connecting the tailpiece pipe and the drain pipe, respectively, thereto for ensuring a leak-proof coupling. Moreover, at least one sealable drain orifice is configured at the at least one inclined face of the tapered closed end.

outputs.L2: A bottle trap is described that includes a main body with an open end connected to a tailpiece pipe and a tapered closed end provided with at least one surface angled at a first angle relative to the axis of the main body. The bottle trap further comprises a cylindrical trap member positioned at the open end and projecting axially into the main body for a distance reaching at least halfway along the length of the main body. An outlet opening is formed in the peripheral wall of the main body and extends perpendicular to it, the outlet opening being arranged for connection to a horizontal drain pipe. outputs.L3:
The bottle trap comprises a main body having an open end configured for connection to a tailpiece pipe and an opposite tapered closed end. The tapered closed end includes at least one inclined face, which facilitates drainage and provides a suitable surface for the placement of an auxiliary drain opening.

A cylindrical trap element is received through the open end of the main body and extends axially into the interior of the main body. The trap element extends along at least half of the length of the main body, thereby helping to define the internal flow path and maintain the water seal required for trap operation.

An outlet orifice is formed on the peripheral surface of the main body. The outlet orifice is arranged substantially perpendicular to the main body and is configured for connection to a horizontal drain pipe, allowing wastewater to be discharged from the trap into the drainage system.

Thread-less couplings are provided both at the open end of the main body and at the outlet orifice. These couplings are configured to connect the tailpiece pipe and the horizontal drain pipe, respectively, in a secure and leak-proof manner without requiring threaded engagement. This arrangement simplifies installation and removal while maintaining reliable sealing performance.

At least one sealable drain orifice is located on the inclined face of the tapered closed end. The drain orifice may be opened when required to empty the trap, remove accumulated debris, or perform maintenance, and may be securely sealed during normal use to prevent leakage.
outputs.L4:
A bottle trap is disclosed for use in a plumbing drain assembly to provide a secure, leak-resistant connection between a vertical tailpiece pipe and a generally horizontal drain pipe. The bottle trap includes a main body defining an internal chamber and having a tapered, closed lower end. The tapered closed end assists in collecting and retaining water within the trap, thereby forming an effective water seal that helps prevent sewer gases from passing back through the plumbing fixture.

An internal cylindrical trap element is positioned within the main body to direct the flow of wastewater through the trap in a controlled path. The trap element cooperates with the surrounding chamber of the main body to maintain the required water seal while allowing wastewater to discharge efficiently. The main body further includes an outlet orifice arranged substantially perpendicular to the central axis of the trap body. This outlet orifice is configured to communicate with a horizontal drain pipe so that wastewater entering through the tailpiece pipe is redirected through the bottle trap and discharged into the drainage system.

The bottle trap is configured to receive and couple to a tailpiece pipe extending from a sink, basin, or other plumbing fixture. The coupling structure may be formed without conventional threads, allowing the pipes to be joined by compression, friction-fit, gasketed, or other thread-less sealing arrangements. Such thread-less couplings simplify installation by reducing the need for threaded engagement, alignment, or the use of additional sealing tapes or compounds. The coupling arrangement also helps provide a reliable, leak-proof connection while allowing the trap to be assembled, removed, or serviced with minimal effort.

One or more drain orifices may be provided in the main body, preferably at or near the lower portion of the trap. These drain orifices are sealable by plugs, caps, gaskets, or other removable sealing members. When sealed, the drain orifices maintain the leak-proof integrity of the trap during normal use. When opened, they allow retained water, sediment, debris, or other accumulated material to be discharged from the trap without requiring complete removal of the trap assembly. This feature facilitates cleaning, inspection, and maintenance.

In use, wastewater from the plumbing fixture flows downward through the tailpiece pipe into the bottle trap. The internal cylindrical trap element directs the water into the trap chamber, where a portion of the water is retained to form a barrier against odors and gases. Excess wastewater then passes through the perpendicular outlet orifice and into the connected horizontal drain pipe. The arrangement provides dependable drainage while maintaining the water seal required for sanitary plumbing operation.

The disclosed bottle trap therefore provides a compact and effective plumbing trap assembly with improved sealing, simplified installation, and convenient maintenance. By combining a main body with a tapered closed end, an internal cylindrical trap element, a perpendicular outlet orifice, thread-less pipe couplings, and sealable drain orifices, the design enables secure drainage and reliable coupling of associated pipes in a leak-proof manner. The construction is particularly useful in installations where ease of assembly, serviceability, and long-term sealing performance are desired.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for a bottle trap with a tapered closed end, inclined drain face, cylindrical trap insert, side outlet, and threadless leak-proof couplings.
counterfactuals.output: A bottle trap assembly for sanitary drainage includes a trap body having a generally cylindrical chamber with a tapered closed lower end defining an inclined drain face for directing retained liquid and debris toward a removable trap insert. The trap insert is substantially cylindrical and is received within the chamber to establish a water seal and facilitate cleaning. A side outlet communicates with the chamber for connection to a waste line, while an inlet is arranged for receiving discharge from a basin or fixture. Threadless leak-proof couplings are provided at one or more connection interfaces to permit rapid installation and removal without threaded engagement, the couplings including sealing elements configured to maintain fluid-tight joints under normal drainage conditions. The tapered closed end and inclined drain face reduce sediment accumulation and improve drainage during servicing, while the removable insert and threadless couplings enable simplified maintenance and reliable sealing in a compact bottle trap configuration.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe a new bottle trap design in patent language, emphasizing thread-less couplings at the inlet and outlet and a drain orifice on an angled tapered end face.
counterfactuals.output:
A bottle trap assembly is disclosed comprising a trap body defining an internal water-seal chamber, an inlet coupling portion, an outlet coupling portion, and a removable lower reservoir portion. The inlet coupling portion and the outlet coupling portion are each configured for thread-less connection to corresponding waste-pipe components, thereby permitting rapid installation without threaded nuts, screw collars, or external compression threads.

In one embodiment, the trap body includes an upper inlet socket arranged to receive an inlet tailpiece in a push-fit manner. A resilient sealing element, such as an elastomeric O-ring, lip seal, or annular gasket, is retained within the inlet socket and is configured to sealingly engage an outer cylindrical surface of the inlet tailpiece. The inlet socket may further include a retention formation, such as a snap-fit detent, locking clip, bayonet-free latch, collet, or friction-retaining sleeve, to resist withdrawal of the inlet tailpiece while maintaining a thread-less coupling.

The outlet coupling portion is similarly formed as a thread-less outlet socket arranged to receive or engage an outlet waste pipe. The outlet socket may include an internal seal seat carrying an annular seal and a mechanical retainer configured to secure the outlet waste pipe without rotation of a threaded coupling member. In certain embodiments, the outlet coupling portion is integrally molded with the trap body and projects laterally from the water-seal chamber.

The lower reservoir portion of the bottle trap terminates in an angled tapered end face. The angled tapered end face is inclined relative to a longitudinal axis of the trap body and converges toward a distal lower region, thereby promoting collection and directional discharge of liquid and debris. A drain orifice is formed through the angled tapered end face and communicates with the internal water-seal chamber. The drain orifice may be positioned at or adjacent the lowermost portion of the angled tapered end face such that, when opened, retained water, sediment, or foreign matter is discharged under gravity.

A closure member is provided for selectively sealing the drain orifice. The closure member may comprise a plug, cap, push-fit stopper, elastomeric seal, quarter-turn insert, or snap-retained drain element. In preferred embodiments, the closure member is also thread-less and is removable without unscrewing, thereby enabling tool-free draining and cleaning of the bottle trap. The angled tapered end face directs flow toward the drain orifice and reduces residual standing liquid within the lower portion of the trap when the drain orifice is opened.

In an exemplary construction, the bottle trap assembly comprises a generally cylindrical body having a vertical inlet, a lateral outlet, and a depending collection chamber. The inlet and outlet are each provided with smooth-walled receiving bores and internal sealing rings, such that plumbing tubes can be inserted axially and sealed by compression of the sealing rings rather than by threaded engagement. The depending collection chamber includes a downwardly narrowing tapered terminal wall disposed at an oblique angle, and the drain orifice extends through said terminal wall. The combination of thread-less inlet and outlet couplings with the angled tapered drain face provides a compact bottle trap that is quickly installable, readily serviceable, and capable of efficient clean-out without disassembly from adjacent plumbing.

In claim-style language, the design may be characterized as follows:

1. A bottle trap assembly comprising:  
   a trap body defining an internal chamber configured to maintain a liquid seal;  
   an inlet coupling portion in fluid communication with the internal chamber, the inlet coupling portion comprising a thread-less receiving socket and an annular sealing member configured to sealingly engage an inlet pipe without threaded engagement;  
   an outlet coupling portion in fluid communication with the internal chamber, the outlet coupling portion comprising a thread-less receiving socket and an annular sealing member configured to sealingly engage an outlet pipe without threaded engagement; and  
   a lower end portion having an angled tapered end face, wherein a drain orifice is formed through the angled tapered end face and communicates with the internal chamber.

2. The bottle trap assembly of claim 1, wherein the drain orifice is disposed adjacent a lowermost region of the angled tapered end face.

3. The bottle trap assembly of claim 1, further comprising a removable closure member configured to selectively seal the drain orifice.

4. The bottle trap assembly of claim 3, wherein the removable closure member is retained in the drain orifice by a thread-less coupling.

5. The bottle trap assembly of claim 1, wherein at least one of the inlet coupling portion and the outlet coupling portion includes a snap-fit retainer, collet, locking clip, or resilient retention member configured to resist axial withdrawal of a pipe received therein.

6. The bottle trap assembly of claim 1, wherein the angled tapered end face is inclined relative to a central longitudinal axis of the trap body such that liquid and debris within the lower end portion are directed toward the drain orifice.

7. The bottle trap assembly of claim 1, wherein the inlet coupling portion and outlet coupling portion are devoid of external screw threads and are configured for push-fit installation.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
